يتكون نظام الاطفاء الذاتى بغاز 
Co2 من عدد من الاسطوانات يوجد بداخلها غاز ثانى اكسيد 
 الكربون فى حالته السائلة تحت ضغط 80 بار تقريبا كما يتم وضع هذه الاسطوانات فى 
 مجموعات طبقا لكمية الغاز المطلوبة للاطفاء وتكون كل مجموعة من هذه المجموعات

rows: Equipment: Automatic CO2 gas fire extinguishing system for the Siemens V94.2 VZ2 gas unit, Preussag – Minimax
Issued to: Damietta Combined Cycle Power Station

sections_en.text: The automatic CO2 gas fire extinguishing system consists of a number of cylinders containing carbon dioxide gas in its liquid state under a pressure of approximately 80 bar. The cylinders are arranged in groups according to the quantity of gas required for extinguishing, and each group is dedicated to extinguishing a fire in a specific area matching the volume of gas inside these cylinders. There are extinguishing gas nozzles and flame detectors distributed as shown in the following table:

Each of the flame and heat detectors has two independent lines, and for the fire system to operate a fire alarm signal must come from one of the fire detectors on the first line together with an alarm from one of the fire detectors on the second line. The weight-release solenoid then moves, the fire system operates, and at the same time the emergency trip signal goes from the limit switch to the various components of the unit so that they stop, and the slow-motion (turning gear) system operates to rotate the unit shaft.
When the system operates or is tested, the weight-release solenoid moves and the weight-carrying arm drops down, and the weight-release box is reset to the operating position.

This document was prepared by Eng. Yousry Abdel Halim Abdel Latif, tested by Eng. Wasfy William Nashed – Senior Engineer, Occupational Safety and Health Department – and approved by Eng. Mohamed Mohamed El-Lawandy, General Manager. It was reviewed by Chemist Ahmed El-Sayed Ibrahim and Eng. Soliman Zaki Soliman, General Manager of Quality Assurance and Quality Control, and approved by Eng. Mohamed Mohamed Farag Anan – Head of Damietta Power Station Sector – and Eng. Mohamed Hussein Gomaa, Head of Quality Assurance and Quality Control Sector, East Delta Electricity Production Company.

rows: Open a work order by the Occupational Safety and Health Department
Open the cover of the weight-release box by pressing the cover lock push button
Make sure that solenoid No. 4 is in its normal operating state, i.e. that the solenoid shaft is down

Turn both the safety catch No. 5 and the cam No. 6 together as far as possible clockwise so as to allow the cable-clamping arm of the mechanism fixing cable No. 7 to be returned to the operating position
The clamping arm No. 7 must be fixed on cam No. 6
Turn the safety catch No. 5 further and then fix it on the stop No. 8 of the weight-release arm No. 2
Push the weight-release arm No. 2 down so that safety catch No. 5 is fixed on stop 8; the mechanism No. 9 is then tensioned and the signal switch No. 13 is in the operating position
The upper ball of cable No. 10 must be placed in the spherical recess of the drop arm No. 11, making sure the cable is firmly in place
Hang the lower ball of cable No. 10 on the holder of the cable-clamping arm No. 7
Fix weights No. 12 and the weight-release arm No. 2
Close the cover of the weight-release box and secure it closed with the cover lock push button

Maintenance Procedures Information System

Document No.: FS-046-R0A | Equipment: Automatic CO2 gas fire extinguishing system for the Siemens V94.2 VZ2 gas unit, Preussag – Minimax
Issued to: Damietta Combined Cycle Power Station
Document status: Approved
Date of document approval: 2 July 2008 | Procedure: Resetting the weight-release box
Date of next review: July 2013
Introduction
The automatic CO2 gas fire extinguishing system consists of a number of cylinders containing carbon dioxide gas in its liquid state under a pressure of approximately 80 bar. The cylinders are arranged in groups according to the quantity of gas required for extinguishing, and each group is dedicated to extinguishing a fire in a specific area matching the volume of gas inside these cylinders. There are extinguishing gas nozzles and flame detectors distributed as shown in the following table:
Flame detector | Heat detector | Nozzles | Number of cylinders | 
1 | 4 | 4 | 3 | Right combustion chamber
1 | 4 | 4 | 3 | Left combustion chamber
1 | 4 | 8 | 7 | Oil tank
Each of the flame and heat detectors has two independent lines, and for the fire system to operate a fire alarm signal must come from one of the fire detectors on the first line together with an alarm from one of the fire detectors on the second line. The weight-release solenoid then moves, the fire system operates, and at the same time the emergency trip signal goes from the limit switch to the various components of the unit so that they stop, and the slow-motion (turning gear) system operates to rotate the unit shaft.
When the system operates or is tested, the weight-release solenoid moves and the weight-carrying arm drops down, and the weight-release box is reset to the operating position.
This document was prepared by Eng. Yousry Abdel Halim Abdel Latif, tested by Eng. Wasfy William Nashed – Senior Engineer, Occupational Safety and Health Department – and approved by Eng. Mohamed Mohamed El-Lawandy, General Manager. It was reviewed by Chemist Ahmed El-Sayed Ibrahim and Eng. Soliman Zaki Soliman, General Manager of Quality Assurance and Quality Control, and approved by Eng. Mohamed Mohamed Farag Anan – Head of Damietta Power Station Sector – and Eng. Mohamed Hussein Gomaa, Head of Quality Assurance and Quality Control Sector, East Delta Electricity Production Company.
Safety Precautions
Open a work order by the Occupational Safety and Health Department | 
Wear personal protective equipment | 
Tools, Equipment and Instruments Used
Pliers – set of screwdrivers | 
Procedure to be Carried Out
Open the cover of the weight-release box by pressing the cover lock push button | 1.
Make sure that solenoid No. 4 is in its normal operating state, i.e. that the solenoid shaft is down | 2.
Turn both the safety catch No. 5 and the cam No. 6 together as far as possible clockwise so as to allow the cable-clamping arm of the mechanism fixing cable No. 7 to be returned to the operating position | 3.
The clamping arm No. 7 must be fixed on cam No. 6 | 4.
Turn the safety catch No. 5 further and then fix it on the stop No. 8 of the weight-release arm No. 2 | 5.
Push the weight-release arm No. 2 down so that safety catch No. 5 is fixed on stop 8; the mechanism No. 9 is then tensioned and the signal switch No. 13 is in the operating position | 6.
The upper ball of cable No. 10 must be placed in the spherical recess of the drop arm No. 11, making sure the cable is firmly in place | 7.
Hang the lower ball of cable No. 10 on the holder of the cable-clamping arm No. 7 | 8
Fix weights No. 12 and the weight-release arm No. 2 | 9
Close the cover of the weight-release box and secure it closed with the cover lock push button | 10
